solution:
The perpendicular distance of a point \((x_1,y_1,z_1)\) from the plane \(ax+by+cz+k=0\) is
\(\dfrac{|ax_1+by_1+cz_1+k|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}\).

Here the point is the origin \((0,0,0)\) and the plane is \(6x+2y+3z-7=0\), so \(a=6,\ b=2,\ c=3,\ k=-7\).

\(\text{Distance}=\dfrac{|6(0)+2(0)+3(0)-7|}{\sqrt{6^2+2^2+3^2}}=\dfrac{|-7|}{\sqrt{36+4+9}}=\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{49}}=\dfrac{7}{7}=1.\)

\(\therefore\) The perpendicular distance of the origin from the plane is \(1\) unit.

The plane is \(2x+3y+6z=49\), so its normal direction is \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\), with \(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+6^2}=\sqrt{49}=7\).

The foot of the perpendicular from the origin lies along the normal through the origin, so its position vector is \(t\,\bar{n}=(2t,\ 3t,\ 6t)\) for some scalar \(t\).

Since this point lies on the plane, substitute into \(2x+3y+6z=49\):
\(2(2t)+3(3t)+6(6t)=49\)
\(4t+9t+36t=49\)
\(49t=49\ \Rightarrow\ t=1.\)

Hence the foot of the perpendicular is \((2(1),\ 3(1),\ 6(1))=(2,\ 3,\ 6)\).

\(\therefore\) The coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular are \((2,\ 3,\ 6)\).

The angle \(\theta\) between two planes equals the angle between their normal vectors.

For \(\bar{r}\cdot(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=17\), the normal is \(\bar{n_1}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\).
For \(\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=71\), the normal is \(\bar{n_2}=2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).

\(\bar{n_1}\cdot\bar{n_2}=(-2)(2)+(1)(2)+(2)(1)=-4+2+2=0.\)

Since \(\bar{n_1}\cdot\bar{n_2}=0\), the normals are perpendicular, so
\(\cos\theta=\dfrac{|\bar{n_1}\cdot\bar{n_2}|}{|\bar{n_1}||\bar{n_2}|}=0\ \Rightarrow\ \theta=90^{\circ}.\)

\(\therefore\) The angle between the two planes is \(90^{\circ}\) (the planes are perpendicular).

The angle \(\theta\) between a line with direction \(\bar{b}\) and a plane with normal \(\bar{n}\) is given by
\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}|}{|\bar{b}||\bar{n}|}.\)

Here the line \(\bar{r}=\lambda(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\) has direction \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), and the plane \(\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=23\) has normal \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).

\(\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}=(1)(2)+(-1)(-1)+(1)(1)=2+1+1=4.\)
\(|\bar{b}|=\sqrt{1^2+(-1)^2+1^2}=\sqrt{3},\quad |\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+1^2}=\sqrt{6}.\)

\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|4|}{\sqrt{3}\cdot\sqrt{6}}=\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{18}}=\dfrac{4}{3\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}.\)

\(\therefore\ \theta=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)\) is the required acute angle.

Comparing with \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda\bar{b_1}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\mu\bar{b_2}\):
\(\bar{a_1}=\hat{i}+4\hat{j}=(1,4,0),\quad \bar{b_1}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}=(1,2,3),\)
\(\bar{a_2}=3\hat{j}-\hat{k}=(0,3,-1),\quad \bar{b_2}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}=(2,3,4).\)

The two lines are coplanar iff \((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=0.\)

\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=(0-1,\ 3-4,\ -1-0)=(-1,-1,-1).\)

\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&2&3\\2&3&4\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(2\cdot4-3\cdot3)-\hat{j}(1\cdot4-3\cdot2)+\hat{k}(1\cdot3-2\cdot2)\)
\(=\hat{i}(8-9)-\hat{j}(4-6)+\hat{k}(3-4)=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}=(-1,2,-1).\)

\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(-1)(-1)+(-1)(2)+(-1)(-1)=1-2+1=0.\)

Since the scalar triple product is \(0\), the lines are coplanar.

The plane containing them has normal \(\bar{n}=\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\) and passes through \(\bar{a_1}=(1,4,0)\).
Using \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a_1}\cdot\bar{n}\):
\(\bar{a_1}\cdot\bar{n}=(1)(-1)+(4)(2)+(0)(-1)=-1+8+0=7.\)

\(\therefore\) Vector equation of the plane: \(\bar{r}\cdot(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})=7\), i.e. \(\bar{r}\cdot(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=-7\).
Cartesian form: \(x-2y+z+7=0\).

The distance of a point with position vector \(\bar{a}\) from the plane \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=d\) is
\(\dfrac{|\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}-d|}{|\bar{n}|}.\)

Here \(\bar{a}=3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}=(3,3,1)\), \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}=(2,3,6)\), and \(d=21\).

\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(3)(2)+(3)(3)+(1)(6)=6+9+6=21.\)
\(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+6^2}=\sqrt{49}=7.\)

\(\text{Distance}=\dfrac{|21-21|}{7}=\dfrac{0}{7}=0.\)

\(\therefore\) The distance is \(0\); the given point lies on the plane.

The distance of a point \((x_1,y_1,z_1)\) from the plane \(ax+by+cz-d=0\) is
\(\dfrac{|ax_1+by_1+cz_1-d|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}.\)

Here the point is \((13,13,-13)\) and the plane is \(3x+4y-12z=0\), so \(a=3,\ b=4,\ c=-12,\ d=0\).

\(ax_1+by_1+cz_1=3(13)+4(13)-12(-13)=39+52+156=247.\)
\(\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}=\sqrt{3^2+4^2+(-12)^2}=\sqrt{9+16+144}=\sqrt{169}=13.\)

\(\text{Distance}=\dfrac{|247|}{13}=\dfrac{247}{13}=19.\)

\(\therefore\) The distance of the point from the plane is \(19\) units.

Write each pair of equations as a line.

Line 1: \(x=y,\ z=0\). Points satisfy \(x=y,\ z=0\); taking parameter \(t\), a point is \((t,t,0)\). It passes through the origin \((0,0,0)\) and has direction \(\bar{b_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}=(1,1,0)\).

Line 2: \(x+y=0,\ z=0\), i.e. \(x=-y,\ z=0\). A point is \((s,-s,0)\). It also passes through the origin \((0,0,0)\) and has direction \(\bar{b_2}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}=(1,-1,0)\).

Both lines pass through the common point \((0,0,0)\), hence they intersect (at the origin).

The plane determined by them has normal
\(\bar{n}=\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&0\\1&-1&0\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(1\cdot0-0\cdot(-1))-\hat{j}(1\cdot0-0\cdot1)+\hat{k}(1\cdot(-1)-1\cdot1)\)
\(=\hat{i}(0)-\hat{j}(0)+\hat{k}(-2)=-2\hat{k}.\)

Taking the normal as \(\hat{k}\), and since the plane passes through the origin, \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{0}\cdot\hat{k}=0\).

\(\therefore\) Vector equation of the plane: \(\bar{r}\cdot\hat{k}=0\) (i.e. the plane \(z=0\)).

The angle \(\theta\) between two planes equals the angle between their normals, given by
\(\cos\theta=\dfrac{|\bar{n_1}\cdot\bar{n_2}|}{|\bar{n_1}||\bar{n_2}|}.\)

For \(\bar{r}\cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=13\): \(\bar{n_1}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}=(1,1,2).\)
For \(\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=31\): \(\bar{n_2}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}=(2,-1,1).\)

\(\bar{n_1}\cdot\bar{n_2}=(1)(2)+(1)(-1)+(2)(1)=2-1+2=3.\)
\(|\bar{n_1}|=\sqrt{1^2+1^2+2^2}=\sqrt{6},\quad |\bar{n_2}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+1^2}=\sqrt{6}.\)

\(\cos\theta=\dfrac{|3|}{\sqrt{6}\cdot\sqrt{6}}=\dfrac{3}{6}=\dfrac{1}{2}.\)

\(\therefore\ \theta=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=60^{\circ}.\)

The angle between the planes is \(60^{\circ}\).

(Note: the line is taken as \(\bar{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-6\hat{k})\); the printed \(\cdot\) between the two vectors is a misprint. Only the direction of the line matters for the angle.)

The angle \(\theta\) between a line with direction \(\bar{b}\) and a plane with normal \(\bar{n}\) is
\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}|}{|\bar{b}||\bar{n}|}.\)

Here \(\bar{b}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-6\hat{k}=(2,3,-6)\) and the plane \(\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=0\) has normal \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}=(2,-1,1).\)

\(\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n}=(2)(2)+(3)(-1)+(-6)(1)=4-3-6=-5.\)
\(|\bar{b}|=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+(-6)^2}=\sqrt{49}=7,\quad |\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+1^2}=\sqrt{6}.\)

\(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|-5|}{7\cdot\sqrt{6}}=\dfrac{5}{7\sqrt{6}}=\dfrac{5\sqrt{6}}{42}.\)

\(\therefore\ \theta=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{5}{7\sqrt{6}}\right)=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{5\sqrt{6}}{42}\right)\) is the required acute angle.

Comparing with \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_1}+\lambda\bar{b_1}\) and \(\bar{r}=\bar{a_2}+\mu\bar{b_2}\):
\(\bar{a_1}=2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}=(0,2,-3),\quad \bar{b_1}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}=(1,2,3),\)
\(\bar{a_2}=2\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+3\hat{k}=(2,6,3),\quad \bar{b_2}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}=(2,3,4).\)

The lines are coplanar iff \((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=0.\)

\(\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1}=(2-0,\ 6-2,\ 3-(-3))=(2,4,6).\)

\(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&2&3\\2&3&4\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(2\cdot4-3\cdot3)-\hat{j}(1\cdot4-3\cdot2)+\hat{k}(1\cdot3-2\cdot2)\)
\(=\hat{i}(8-9)-\hat{j}(4-6)+\hat{k}(3-4)=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}=(-1,2,-1).\)

\((\bar{a_2}-\bar{a_1})\cdot(\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2})=(2)(-1)+(4)(2)+(6)(-1)=-2+8-6=0.\)

Since the scalar triple product is \(0\), the lines are coplanar.

The plane has normal \(\bar{n}=\bar{b_1}\times\bar{b_2}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\) and passes through \(\bar{a_1}=(0,2,-3)\).
\(\bar{a_1}\cdot\bar{n}=(0)(-1)+(2)(2)+(-3)(-1)=0+4+3=7.\)

\(\therefore\) Vector equation: \(\bar{r}\cdot(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})=7\), i.e. \(\bar{r}\cdot(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=-7\).
Cartesian form: \(x-2y+z+7=0\).

The distance of a point \(\bar{a}\) from the plane \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=d\) is \(\dfrac{|\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}-d|}{|\bar{n}|}.\)

Here \(\bar{a}=4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}=(4,-3,1)\), \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-6\hat{k}=(2,3,-6)\), and \(d=21\).

\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(4)(2)+(-3)(3)+(1)(-6)=8-9-6=-7.\)
\(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+3^2+(-6)^2}=\sqrt{49}=7.\)

\(\text{Distance}=\dfrac{|-7-21|}{7}=\dfrac{|-28|}{7}=\dfrac{28}{7}=4.\)

\(\therefore\) The distance of the point from the plane is \(4\) units.

The distance of a point \((x_1,y_1,z_1)\) from the plane \(ax+by+cz+k=0\) is
\(\dfrac{|ax_1+by_1+cz_1+k|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}.\)

Here the point is \((1,1,-1)\) and the plane is \(3x+4y-12z+20=0\), so \(a=3,\ b=4,\ c=-12,\ k=20\).

\(ax_1+by_1+cz_1+k=3(1)+4(1)-12(-1)+20=3+4+12+20=39.\)
\(\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}=\sqrt{3^2+4^2+(-12)^2}=\sqrt{9+16+144}=\sqrt{169}=13.\)

\(\text{Distance}=\dfrac{|39|}{13}=\dfrac{39}{13}=3.\)

\(\therefore\) The distance of the point from the plane is \(3\) units.
